english.notes:
(i) Section 105 of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 makes special provisions for this offence in relation to ships and aircraft.
(ii) Section 106 of the Act applies where a person is convicted of this offence and the contravention continues after the conviction.
(iii) Section 107 of the Act provides for proceedings and enforcement where this offence has been committed in UK territorial sea.
(iv) Section 110 of the Act provides for criminal liability of company directors, managers, etc.
(v) Schedule 4 of the Act provides for fixed penalty notices for this offence.
(vi) The Wireless Telegraphy (Fixed Penalty) Regulations 2011 introduced a £100 fixed penalty charge for summary only offences under the Act from 1st October 2011. This regime does not include offences relating to illegal broadcasting (pirate radio).

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 51 weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

The amount of the fixed penalty is £100, see paragraph 2 of Schedule 4 to the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 and regulations 2 and 3 of the Wireless Telegraphy (Fixed Penalty) Regulations 2011 (in force from 1st October 2011).

For offences committed before the commencement of section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003, the reference to imprisonment of 51 weeks is to be read as six months, paragraph 18 of Schedule 8 to the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months
